chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you arrive at the Haram, if God wills, perform the ritual bath (ghusl) upon entering it. And if you perform it beforehand, then perform the bath from the Well of Maymoun, or from Fakh, or from your house in Mecca.
ai.seo_question: What is the proper source of water for the ritual bath before entering the Haram in Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi emphasizes the spiritual preparation for entering the Haram, prescribing a ritual bath (ghusl) to ensure physical and spiritual purity. It offers practical flexibility by allowing the ghusl to be performed earlier using water from the Well of Maymoun, Fakh, or one's residence in Mecca, reflecting the scholarly tradition of accommodating travelers' circumstances while maintaining the sanctity of the sacred precinct.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Whenever you end up to the Harram, Allahazwj Willing, so wash where you enter it (on arrival). And, if you were to wash beforehand, so wash from the well of Maymoun, or from Fakkha, or from you house in Makkah’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

when you, by the will of Allah, enter al-Haram (the sacred area), take a shower upon your arrival; but if you take it before your arrival, then take a shower in Bi’r Maymun (name of a place) or in Fakhkh or in your lodging in Makkah.’”
